transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep hearing voices, and it’s gotten to where I can’t just brush it off anymore. It’s not like a thought in my head or like remembering somebody’s voice — it sounds clear, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio with me. The house will be quiet, nobody’s there, and I’ll hear my name, plain as anything.

And sometimes it’s not just my name. They’ll say things about my work being judged, like people are looking at what I’m doing or measuring it somehow. I know that sounds strange saying it out loud, but when it happens it feels so real, like I should be able to turn around and see someone there. It’s been scaring me, honestly, and I didn’t know what else to do but come in.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being controlled or that people are watching or following you in ways that don’t make sense to others?

Yes… yes, I have felt that. Not so much like somebody has a remote control on my thoughts, but more like people are watching what I’m doing, and I can’t shake it even when other people tell me it doesn’t add up.

It started getting really fixed in my mind that the other home-care agency — the one that does similar work, you know — and even some people from the library were keeping tabs on me. I know that sounds like a lot when I say “library people,” but that’s how it felt. Like they were looking at my paintings, watching what I was making, and also somehow paying attention to my client papers. And I felt like they were doing it because there was some chance meant for me, something I was supposed to get, and they were trying to steal it before I could.

People would tell me, “That doesn’t make sense, why would they do that?” but it didn’t really change what I knew in my gut. I kept thinking, no, they’re doing it, they’re watching, they’re waiting for me to slip up or take what was mine. It made me feel on edge all the time, like I had to protect everything.

Have you ever felt that things happening around you were directly related to you in a special or unusual way, like events or messages were meant specifically for you or pointed to something important about your role or destiny?

Yes… that happened a lot, honestly. I started feeling like things were lining up around me for a reason, like it wasn’t just regular life anymore. I really believed my artwork was about to be discovered any day, like somebody important was going to see it and realize it was something special. Not just “oh, that’s nice,” but like it was meant to become bigger, like I had a purpose with it.

And it wasn’t only the paintings by themselves. I had this whole idea in my head that I was supposed to make a new kind of program, like combining care work and art together — for older people, for people who needed help, you know, something that would make them feel seen and calm and creative. And I really, truly believed doctors and agencies were going to come learn it from me. Like they would come to me and say, “How did you figure this out?” and I’d be the one showing them.

At the time it didn’t feel far-fetched. It felt clear, like I was being shown that this was my role, that I was supposed to build this whole care-and-art thing and other people were going to recognize it. Looking back, I guess it sounds like a lot, but when I was in it, it felt important and real.
Has there been a time when these experiences made it hard for you to take care of everyday things, like work, personal hygiene, or spending time with people?

Yes… it really did. That’s part of what scared me enough to come in, because it wasn’t just happening and then I could still keep everything together. I started slipping in ways I normally don’t.

With my aide work, I missed shifts, and that is not like me — or it didn’t used to be. I’d get mixed up about where I was supposed to be or what time, and then I’d be so preoccupied trying to make sense of things that I couldn’t keep the visits straight. My care notes got messy too. I would write something down and then later I’d look at it and think, “Did I put that under the right person? Did I finish that part?” It got to where I felt like my job was in danger, like they were going to say I couldn’t be trusted with it anymore.

And outside of work, I just kind of disappeared from things. I used to go to my walking club, and I liked the library art talks, even if I didn’t always say much there. But I stopped going. I’d tell myself I was too tired or I needed to stay home and get organized, but really I just stayed in my studio by myself most of the time. So yes, it made everyday life hard — work, keeping up with people, all of it.
Have these experiences — hearing voices and feeling watched — happened mostly on their own, without being tied closely to periods where you were feeling unusually high, low, or depressed?

Yes… yes, I think they did happen on their own too. That’s something I’ve been trying to sort out, because at first I thought maybe it was only when I was really wound up or not sleeping right, like everything was moving too fast in my head. But there was a period after that where my energy had dropped back down and I was sleeping more normal again — not perfect, but more like regular sleep — and the voices still didn’t just stop.

And the feeling of being watched, or judged, or like people were tracking my work… that kept going too. It wasn’t like, “Oh, I’m calmer now, so I can see none of that is happening.” It stayed with me for weeks. I’d be going about my day, not especially up or anything, and still feel like people were looking at what I was doing, checking my work, judging the papers or the art or whatever I had touched. It kept sitting there in my mind even when the rest of me had slowed down.

So yes, I guess that’s the answer — it wasn’t only tied to feeling high or really low. It kept going even after that shifted.
Have there been times when you experienced these strange beliefs or feelings of being watched without any significant changes in your mood, like when you weren’t feeling especially high or low?

Yes, that did happen. I know I sort of said it already, but… it’s important because it wasn’t only when I was really up or really down.

There was a stretch after my energy came back down some — like I wasn’t racing around the same way, and I was sleeping more like a normal person again, or closer to normal anyway — and even then, the voices didn’t just disappear. And that feeling that people were watching me, or judging what I was doing, or somehow tracking my work, it kept going.

It went on for several weeks like that. I remember thinking, “Well, I’m not feeling especially high right now, so why is this still happening?” But it still felt real at the time. I could be doing ordinary things, trying to get through the day, and still have that sense that my work was being checked or that people were paying attention to me in a way they shouldn’t be. So yes… it happened even when my mood wasn’t changed in a big way.
Have you ever had times when you experienced these strange beliefs or feelings of being watched even when your mood was completely stable and not unusually high or low at all?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I’m careful saying “completely stable,” because I don’t always know how to measure that in myself, but there was definitely a time after that more wound-up feeling had dropped off. My energy came down, and I wasn’t staying up like before — I was sleeping more normally, more like my usual pattern.

But even then, the voices didn’t stop right away. And the idea that people were judging me or tracking my work, like checking what I was doing or looking at things I had touched or written, that kept going too. It wasn’t just a day or two. It went on for several weeks after my mood felt more settled.

That’s what confused me, honestly. I kept thinking, if I’m not especially high or low right now, why does it still feel like this is happening? But it did. It still felt real during that time.
Can you think back to a time when your mood was completely normal—neither high nor low—and during that time, did you still experience the voices or the feeling of being watched?

Yes… yes, I can think of a time like that. I know I’ve said pieces of this already, but that’s the part that really sticks in my mind, because it didn’t match what I thought should happen.

There was a period after my energy had dropped back down. I wasn’t feeling all sped up like before, and I was sleeping more normally again — not saying everything was perfect, but I was closer to my usual self. I wasn’t in that high, restless place, and I wasn’t feeling especially low either.

But the voices were still there. They didn’t just shut off because my mood evened out. And that feeling that people were watching me or judging me, especially around my work or things I had done or touched, that kept going too. It felt like people were tracking it somehow, like checking behind me or paying attention in a way that didn’t feel normal.

And it wasn’t just for one afternoon or one bad night. It went on for several weeks after I felt more normal mood-wise. That’s what scared me, I think, because I kept thinking, “If I’m calmer now, why is this still happening?” But it was still there.
